memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Also make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle, five for those on the other side, and five for the frames on the west, at the far end of the tabernacle. The centre crossbar is to extend from end to end at the middle of the frames. Overlay the frames with gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Also overlay the crossbars with gold." - Exodus 26:26-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The upright frames needed something more: crossbars running horizontally through gold rings, binding the whole structure together. And one bar was different — the centre crossbar ran the full length, end to end, holding everything in a single continuous line. Without it, the frames would stand but sway.

We all need crossbars. Uprightness alone is not enough; we need what binds and steadies us over the long run. Convictions, habits of prayer, faithful friendships, regular time in Scripture — these run through our lives horizontally, holding things together when pressure comes from one side or another.

And there is a centre bar, running the full length. For the believer, that is Christ Himself, who holds all things together (Col 1:17) and remains the same yesterday, today, and forever (Heb 13:8). Whatever else changes across the length of your life — seasons, circumstances, strength, health — He runs through the whole of it, unchanging. If your life feels unsteady, ask what crossbars are missing. And whatever else you strengthen, make sure the centre bar is firmly in place.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What "crossbars" of habit and relationship are steadying my life?
Is Christ genuinely the centre bar running through the whole of my life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You hold all things together and never change. Run through the whole length of my life as my centre, and steady me with habits and friendships that keep me firm. Amen.
